title: SDKS samples runway & release-notes synchronization for structured streaming + function-calling
creator: Sophie Kim
description:
Goal: deliver a coordinated runway for SDK samples (JS/TS, Python, Go) and the canonical release notes for two API surface features: structured output and streaming with function-calling. This ticket covers orchestration across Docs, SDKs, Console samples, and Marketing assets, and defines the acceptance criteria for samples to be included in the public release.

Scope and deliverables:
- Canonical sample apps for structured output (chat -> JSON/table) demonstrating schema enforcement and parse validation across SDKs.
- Streaming + function-calling sample that wires a streaming chat response to an external tool call (simulated webhook) with reconnect and chunked events handling.
- Release notes draft with breaking changes table, migration snippets, and per-SDK code diffs.
- Release-ready markdown for docs site + embed-ready snippets for the quickstart.
- Test harness and CI checks that run sample smoke tests against staging runtime-1.22 to validate compatibility.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Timebox: samples must be stable on runtime-1.22 but we will include fallbacks for runtime-1.18 where feature parity differs.
- Prioritize developer clarity over exhaustive coverage: the samples should be opinionated patterns (1 canonical way per language).
- Avoid shipping large tutorial code; link to a compact sample repo instead to speed review.

Success criteria (high level):
- All sample repos pass CI smoke tests in staging and are linked in docs.
- Release notes reviewed and approved by Eng, Docs, Security, and Comms.
- On release day, SDK quickstart snippets render correctly in the docs site and the console snippets work in the staging console playground.

Owners & reviewers:
- PM owner: Sophie Kim (creator) — coordination and sign-off on release notes.
- Lead engineer: Priya Shah (ENG-28102) — runtime compatibility sign-off and CI gating.
- Docs lead: Marco Alvarez (Docs) — sample wording and snippet formatting.
- Design: Lina Park (DES-3045) — approve sample UX for console playground.
- Marketing/Comms reviewer: Elena Rivera — release notes headline and changelog entry.

Artifacts and where to find them (working links):
- Draft release notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SDK-Release-2025-04 (draft)
- Samples repo (canonical): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples/tree/pm-53814
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples/pulls?q=is%3Apr+pm-53814
- Docs staging page (render preview): https://docs-staging.redwood.ai/sdk/structured-output/ (internal preview)
- CI smoke dashboard: https://ci.redwood.ai/pipelines/pm-53814-smoke

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: streaming behavior differs by runtime kernel selection (latency spikes in canary). Mitigation: include a short note in release notes about recommended runtime pinning and an automatic fallback example.
- Risk: function-calling security review misses edge-case on webhook validation. Mitigation: security to run one-off review and we add a checkbox in the release checklist for signed webhook examples.

Notes on coordination:
- Weekly sync cadence with Eng/Docs/Design for the next three sprints (calendar invites created).
- Freeze date for sample API surface is 2025-02-05 (this ticket's updated_at marks the last spec update); after freeze only critical fixes allowed.

Next steps (actionable):
1) ENG: Cut sample branches for each language and gate CI smoke tests (owner: Priya).
2) DOCS: Publish release-notes draft and insert code snippets; create review comments inline (owner: Marco).
3) DESIGN: Provide final console snippet styling by 2025-01-25 (owner: Lina).
4) PM: Lock final release note headlines and approve marketing blurb (owner: Sophie).

Estimated release runway: 3 weeks from created_at (buffered for reviews).
